mintAuthority.summary: Ethereum frxUSD can be minted and redeemed through governance-approved FrxUSDCustodian contracts with per-custodian caps; the token and custodians are owned by the current 4/7 frxUSD owner/custodian admin Safe, while Ethereum proxy upgrades require the same Safe to pass through a 24-hour timelock. Fraxtal frxUSD3 also exposes a direct minter_mint path to an owner/timelock-controlled minter set with no source-level cap or max-supply check; the Fraxtal L2 bridge and canonical-side lockboxes are bridge machinery assessed separately under bridgeRouteRisk, and Tempo remains unresolved.

controls.label: frxUSD upgrade timelock
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, all six frxUSD token/custodian ProxyAdmins returned this verified Compound-style timelock as owner. Its admin() was the 4-of-7 frxUSD owner/custodian admin Safe, pendingAdmin() was zero, and delay() was 86400 seconds; verified source requires the admin to queue upgrades and wait through the delay before execution.

controls.label: frxUSD owner/custodian admin Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, frxUSD token owner(), every listed custodian owner(), and the upgrade timelock admin() returned this Safe. On-chain Safe reads returned version 1.3.0, threshold 4, the seven listed owners, no enabled modules, zero guard, and zero moduleGuard.

controls.label: Fraxtal frxUSD owner/timelock contract
controls.capDescription: FrxUSD3 inherits ERC20PermitPermissionedOptiMintable: minter_mint() has no source-level cap or max-supply invariant; owner()/timelock_address() controls the minter set, and the separate Fraxtal ProxyAdmin is owner-controlled. Total supply at the fixed review block was 14408997.267859968047907063 frxUSD.
controls.evidence: At Fraxtal block 40053263, owner() and timelock_address() on 0xfc00000000000000000000000000000000000001 both returned 0xc4eb45d80dc1f079045e75d5d55de8ed1c1090e6, and minters(0xc4eb45d80dc1f079045e75d5d55de8ed1c1090e6) returned true. The reviewed FrxUSD2 and ERC20PermitPermissionedOptiMintable source shows that an active minter can call minter_mint() directly, while the owner/timelock can manage minters; no cap or max-supply check appears on that path.

controls.label: Fraxtal frxUSD active minter 0xfc...000d
controls.capDescription: The active minter_mint() path has no source-level cap or max-supply check. This address exposes proxy/system-like upgrade selectors, but its exact identity, owner, upgrade configuration, and ability to alter mint economics remain unresolved.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25546949, the frxUSD token and all five custodian proxies published by Frax resolved distinct EIP-1967 implementations and ProxyAdmins. Every ProxyAdmin had identical verified runtime and owner() = 0xb898Ad2976b4d8f2E21521C9db16b7497825E503. That verified timelock had admin 0xfFFffF4F3baC444b2C0ecf2A1840d018bE783937, pendingAdmin zero, and a 86400-second delay. The same 4-of-7 Safe directly owned the token and every custodian, could raise their mint caps, and had no enabled modules, guard, or module guard. This establishes the complete published Ethereum token/custodian upgrade and mint-control chain; replacing mint-critical logic requires the Safe-controlled 24-hour timelock. At Fraxtal block 40053263, native frxUSD at 0xfc00000000000000000000000000000000000001 returned BRIDGE() = 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010, REMOTE_TOKEN() = 0xcacd6fd266af91b8aed52accc382b4e165586e29, owner() = timelock_address() = 0xc4eb45d80dc1f079045e75d5d55de8ed1c1090e6, and active minters 0xc4eb45d80dc1f079045e75d5d55de8ed1c1090e6, 0xfc0000000000000000000000000000000000000d, 0x96a394058e2b84a89bac9667b19661ed003cf5d4, and 0x8c33cd6e5bed3bcb43b116410842bdd21630bff4. The reviewed source has no cap or max-supply check on minter_mint(); the Fraxtal ProxyAdmin owner/delay is not independently resolved, so the Ethereum 86400-second delay is not applied to Fraxtal. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-16: the Ethereum Safe can raise custodian caps directly outside the upgrade timelock, Fraxtal owner-controlled minters can mint without a source-level economic bound, and the live full-composition Frax/Chaos reserve feed provides continuous third-party reconciliation without named prudential supervision.
